newsitem.title: USA: Stocks seen hit at opening by Intel.
newsitem.headline: Stocks seen hit at opening by Intel.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were expected to fall sharply Friday, hurt by predictions by chip maker Intel Corp. that its second-quarter results would be below expectations.
Analysts said Intel's announcement would pummel the technology sector and that a collapse there could weigh on the entire market,
In trading on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, the Standard & Poor's 500 stock index futures fell sharply, with the June contract down 12.9 points at 832.6.
Traders said a decline of that size would indicate a fall of more than 100 points in the Dow Jones industrial average.
"It's batten down the hatches time. We're likely to see the tech sector ripped apart today," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.
Intel was trading at $145.50 in third-market after closing Thursday at $163.76 on Nasdaq.
Analysts also said revised gross domestic product figures for the first quarter were in line with expectations and should have little effect on the opening.
The government revised growth to 5.8 percent, up slightly from the initial figure of 5.6 percent.
